intro: The route has thirty-two steps in eight bands. Each mark enters with the first word that needs it, and the verb kernel runs through every band. The orientation map shows the same route with each word's letters in colour.

steps.title: Open or closed
steps.words_md: *I* / *it, in, is, if*; contrast *I/it, I/in*
steps.marks: sound circle, syllable swoop, long, short
steps.carney: Short vowels can't end an open syllable and long vowels can, p. 134; short i, p. 135; long i, p. 151

steps.title: Closed two-letter words
steps.words_md: *at, an, am, as, on, up, us*
steps.marks: none
steps.carney: The short word rule: lexical words usually have at least three letters, and function words can have two, pp. 131–133; short a, p. 143; short u, p. 147; short o, p. 149; *s* for /z/, p. 238
steps.parts_why: A short vowel closed by one consonant, as *at* and *up*.

steps.title: Open vowels spell their names
steps.words_md: *he, me, we, be, my, by, so, no, go*; contrast *go/do, so/to*
steps.marks: none
steps.carney: Long vowels can end an open syllable, p. 134; *be* beside *bee*, p. 133; long e, p. 155; long i, p. 151; long o, p. 171
steps.parts_why: Open, so the vowel spells its name, as *he* and *me*.

steps.title: One consonant closes it
steps.words_md: *be/bed, me/met, we/wet, go/got, no/not, hi/him/hit*; contrast *so/sob*
steps.marks: none
steps.carney: Short vowels, p. 134; each short vowel, pp. 135–150
steps.parts_why: One consonant closes it, as *bed* and *not*.

steps.title: Two letters, one sound
steps.words_md: *the, she, this, that, with, much, such, which*; contrast *she/shed*
steps.marks: green bond bar
steps.carney: *h* as a helper (auxiliary) letter in *ch*, *sh* and *ph*, p. 39; *ch*, p. 226; *th*, p. 232; *sh*, p. 240; *wh*, p. 253

steps.title: Closed words in the kernel
steps.words_md: *has, had, did, can, will, shall, must, get, went, spell*
steps.marks: black bond bar on doubled endings (*will*, *spell*); the box comes with endings at step 14
steps.kernel_md: *has, had, did, can, will, shall, must, get, went*
steps.carney: At the end of a word, doubling is largely limited to *ff*, *ss*, *ll*, *ck*, *tch* and *dge* (rule #D5), p. 123; *add*, *egg* and the short word rule, pp. 123, 131
steps.parts_why: Closed, with two consonants after the vowel, as *must* and *spell*.

steps.title: One analog, three words
steps.words_md: *would* → *could, should*
steps.marks: red bond bar
steps.carney: *ou* for the vowel of *book* in *could*, *should* and *would*, p. 146; their empty *l*, p. 249; rule O.22, p. 346

steps.title: The *e* that keeps *v* off the end
steps.words_md: *have, has, had*; *give/gave*; *live/live*
steps.marks: cone of silence; vowel vault in *gave*
steps.carney: The *e* after *v* in *have* and *love*, p. 13; *ve* as the doubled *v*, p. 121; no final *v* (*nerve*, *serve*), p. 189; a final *v* only in short forms and slang (*gov*, *rev*), p. 231

steps.title: The vault
steps.words_md: *make, like, time, home, name*; contrast *mad/made, dim/dime, hop/hope, not/note, cub/cube*
steps.marks: the vault on every vowel–consonant–*e* word
steps.carney: The *e* marks a long vowel, p. 129; *matting* beside *mating*, p. 114
steps.parts_why: The final e sends the vault, as *home* and *name*.

steps.title: The nice-nudge
steps.words_md: *nice, face, place, age, page, huge*; contrast *cap/cape/face, rag/rage*
steps.marks: nice-nudge
steps.carney: *c* spells /s/ before *e* (rule C.8), p. 303; *g* spells /j/ before *e*, *i* and *y* (rules G.9 and G.12), pp. 326–327
steps.parts_why: The final e nudges the c soft, as *nice*; in *duce* it sends the vault too.

steps.title: Vowel teams
steps.words_md: *may, day, see, been, might, night*
steps.marks: none
steps.carney: Long a, p. 164; long e, p. 155; *igh*, p. 154

steps.title: The r-controlled unit
steps.words_md: *or, for, her, are, were, car, bird, turn*
steps.marks: r-controlled unit
steps.parts_why: A vowel and r as one unit, as *her* and *for*.

steps.title: A suffix joins at the seam
steps.words_md: *gets, sees, going, doing, being**, played*
steps.marks: morpheme seam
steps.carney: *-ed* and *-s* keep one spelling, pp. 18–19 (table 5); *ng*, p. 248
steps.parts_why: The suffixes this step joins at the seam.

steps.title: The box blocks the vault
steps.words_md: *spell/spelling, get/getting, **help/helped, **sun/sunny, happy*
steps.marks: block box and blocked vault, where two consonants stop a reach, doubled or already there (*spelling*, *getting**, helped*)
steps.carney: Doubling marks a short vowel, p. 114; *ck*, *tch* and *dge* as the doubled spellings (rule #D3), p. 121; *tch* as the doubled *ch*, p. 226

steps.title: The *e* drops, its jobs move
steps.words_md: *make/making, have/having, race/racing, ice/icy*; contrast *hoping/hopping, filing/filling*
steps.marks: none: the vault and nudge move to the suffix vowel
steps.carney: The *e* drops before an ending that begins with a vowel, p. 130, and stays where it still nudges *c* or *g* (*noticeable*), p. 131

steps.title: Open and closed in longer words
steps.words_md: long: *tiger, paper, music, open*; short: *seven, lemon, robin*; weak: *today, around*; contrast *even/seven, robot/robin, tiger/river, silent/silly*
steps.marks: none: a long first vowel takes the vault, a short one takes the consonant into its syllable (*sev·en*), and a weak one stays bare
steps.carney: In a vowel-consonant-vowel run the first vowel is often short, and hard to predict without stress, p. 275; open syllables, p. 134
steps.move: Try the first vowel long, then short, then weak. Keep the one that makes a word you know, then mark it.
steps.research: Kearns (2020): with one consonant between two vowels, the first vowel of a two-syllable word is long 47% of the time, short 25% and weak 21%. In longer words it is long only 19% of the time. The vowel matters: *u* is usually long (84%), and *e* is long only 18% of the time and weak 60%.
steps.parts_why: A weak vowel alone in its syllable, as *around*.

steps.title: Consonant + le
steps.words_md: *table, bugle, title, little, apple, middle*; contrast *title/little, table/apple, bugle/bubble*
steps.marks: none: a red bond bar and one red circle under *le*
steps.carney: *le* is a vowel and a consonant with the letters switched, p. 129; a short vowel before *le* doubles (*bubble*, *bottle*; rule #D9), p. 124; *le* beside *al*, *el*, *il* and *ol*, p. 433

steps.title: Long before two consonants
steps.words_md: *old, cold, both, most, only, find, kind, child, wild*; contrast *most/cost, mind/mint*
steps.marks: none: the long mark with no vault
steps.carney: Long vowels before *nd*, *ld* and *lt* (*find*, *cold*, *bolt*), p. 129; *old*, *olt* and *oll* words, p. 175; *find*, *kind*, *child* and *wild* (rules I.11 and I.12), pp. 332–333

steps.title: A vowel that borrows a sound
steps.words_md: *come, some, done, from, was, what, do, to, who, does*; contrast *home/come, bone/done/gone*
steps.marks: none: the borrowing vowel stays bare
steps.carney: *o* for *u* beside *m* and *n*, where pen strokes ran together (*come*), p. 69; *a* after *w* (*want*, *wash*, *what*, *was*), p. 150; *do*, *to* and *who*, p. 198

steps.title: Teams for the long vowels
steps.words_md: *rain, paid, eat, read, please, boat, show, grow, own, pie, they, eight*
steps.marks: none
steps.carney: Long a, p. 164; long e, p. 155; long o, p. 171; long i, p. 151

steps.title: The long u sound
steps.words_md: *too, moon, food, new, grew, blue, true, you, soup*; contrast *do/due/dew*
steps.marks: none
steps.carney: Long u, p. 196; long u with a *y* sound before it (*cute*), p. 200

steps.title: A team's second sound
steps.words_md: *look, good, book, head, bread, put, pull, said, again, many*; contrast *moon/book, eat/head*
steps.marks: open: whether a team with two sounds takes a mark
steps.carney: The vowel of *book*, p. 144; *full*, *pull* and *put*, p. 145; short e spelled *ea*, p. 141

steps.title: The aw sound
steps.words_md: *saw, draw, law, because, want, wash, water, all, small, walk*
steps.marks: none
steps.carney: *aw*, *au* and *a* before *l*, pp. 181–182; *all*, *ball* and *call*, p. 184; *a* after *w*, p. 150

steps.title: The ouch and oil sounds
steps.words_md: *out, round, found, how, now, down, coin, point, boy, toy*; contrast *now/snow*
steps.marks: none: *ow* joins the teams with two sounds
steps.carney: *ou* and *ow*, p. 169; *oi* and *oy*, p. 202

steps.title: Silent letters join their unit
steps.words_md: *know, knee, knife, write, wrong, lamb, climb, two*; contrast *knot/not, wrap/rap*
steps.marks: black bond bar for a consonant unit
steps.carney: *kn* and *mb* as units, p. 41; inert and empty letters, pp. 41–42; the *w* of *wring*, p. 44

steps.title: More r-controlled units
steps.words_md: *hair, hear, our, your, their, more, before, care, there, where*; contrast *were/there, are/care*
steps.marks: none: the red bar runs under three letters in *hair*. *Our* splits into the *ou* of *out* and an *r*.
steps.carney: *or*, p. 181; *ear*, p. 190; *air*, and the *ere* of *there* and *where*, pp. 192–194; *ure*, p. 194

steps.title: Two words join
steps.words_md: *I'm, it's, isn't, don't, can't, won't, we're*
steps.marks: red apostrophe for the letters left out
steps.carney: The apostrophe, p. 50

steps.title: The th and wh family
steps.words_md: *this, that, these, those, then, there*; contrast *then/when, there/where, that/what*
steps.marks: proposed: pointer pill
steps.carney: The voiced *th* of *the*, *this*, *these*, *that*, *those*, *then* and *there*, p. 232; the *h* of *whine*, p. 44; *wh*, p. 253

steps.title: -y, -ly and y turns to i
steps.words_md: *sadly, slowly, happily, happier, tried, carries*; contrast *try/tried, play/played*
steps.marks: none: the seam
steps.carney: *-y* and *-ies* (*berry*, *berries*), p. 70; *carry*, *carried*, *carries*, p. 135; *i* before some endings (*happiness*), p. 136

steps.title: un- and re-
steps.words_md: *undo, untie, unhappy, unlock, redo, replay, refill, reread*
steps.marks: none: the seam, before the root
steps.carney: No section of its own. A morpheme keeps its spelling, p. 18; *re-enact* beside *react*, p. 48
steps.parts_why: Back again, now joined to words.

steps.title: A Latin family: act and create
steps.words_md: *act, action, actor, active, react, create, creation, creator*
steps.marks: none
steps.carney: Words from Latin, pp. 96–101; *-tion*, p. 420; *-er* and *-or*, p. 426

steps.title: A Greek family: photo, phone, graph
steps.words_md: *photo, phone, graph, telephone, photograph, alphabet*
steps.marks: none: the black bond bar under *ph*
steps.carney: *ph* in words from Greek, p. 228; words from Greek, pp. 96–101

carney_intro: Edward Carney's *A Survey of English Spelling* (Routledge, 1994) describes every unit on the route, and the atlas leans on it from the first step to the last. The pages are Carney's printed pages; a sound named on its own is the start of his section on that sound. How a phonics program lines up with the route is in a crosswalk, a separate PDF for each program. The first is for UFLI Foundations.
moves_intro: Some steps teach a move: what a learner tries when the marks alone don't settle a word. Each move is listed with the research behind it. Devin M. Kearns, "Does English Have Useful Syllable Division Patterns?" *Reading Research Quarterly* 55, no. S1 (2020): S145–S160, counted how the vowels are said in 14,844 words from texts for grades 1 to 8. His figures describe the words, not learners. Added 10 November 2026.
parts_intro: The commonest prefixes and suffixes, and the roots the families use, each placed at the step whose pattern it shows, so a part met on the route is met again in its families. Each is marked as it is said on its own. Inside a word many are said weakly, as the *con* of the verb *conduct* is, and there the vowel would be bare. Added 10 November 2026.
open: Teams with two sounds (steps 22 and 24). The Orton-Gillingham manual puts a bar or a cup over *oo* (p. 17), and the vicinity pattern page says a team takes no long mark, short mark or vault. The marking calls of 7 October mark both sounds alike for now.
Step 19 could move up to follow step 13. Its words are met in marked text from rung 1, and every unit it uses is in place by step 13, where the seam lets *does* be built as *do* + *es*.
The black bond bar enters the map's key at step 25, but *qu* (step 4), *wh* (step 5) and *ng* (step 13) already take it on the cards and in the appendix. The key could name it at step 5.
The pointer pill at step 28 is a proposed mark, not a decided one.
note_16_32:
Steps 16 to 32 were added as a draft on 15 October 2026, and the orientation map shows them in the same form. The new bands repeat the first four at a larger scale: single vowels, then teams, then the remaining units, then words built from parts.
With the same script and assumptions as the ELP table, 144 of the 148 ELP words are readable by step 26. *Of, laugh, pretty* and *people* stay one-offs. In adult text (wordfreq, top 6,000 words), the share of running words readable on the route rises from about 46% at step 15 to about 70% at step 26.
